label: Germany
goalHint: Reach {majority} of {total} seats, alone or in a compatible coalition. The 5% national threshold can exclude parties; CSU is exempt.

issues.name: Economy & industry
issues.blurb: Growth, unemployment, the cost of energy and the future of German industry.

issues.name: Migration
issues.blurb: Asylum, border control and how many newcomers the country can take in.

issues.name: Security & defence
issues.blurb: NATO, the Bundeswehr's missions abroad, defence spending and Russia.

issues.name: Energy & climate
issues.blurb: Nuclear power, coal, the energy transition and what it costs.

issues.name: Pensions & welfare
issues.blurb: An ageing society and the future of the social state.

issues.name: Housing & rents
issues.blurb: Rents and house prices in the big cities.

1990.label: 1990 · Kohl v. Lafontaine
1990.tagline: December 2, 1990. The first free all-German election since 1932, two months after unification. Kohl has the credit for unity, and Lafontaine is the candidate who asked what it would cost. East and West have separate 5 percent thresholds, so the PDS and the East's civil rights alliance need only their own half to get in.

events.headline: Monetary union on July 1 swaps East German marks for Deutschmarks one to one for wages and small savings, and {party} takes the credit
Kohl promises unity without tax rises and 'blooming landscapes' in the East within a few years, and {party} rides the optimism
Lafontaine warns that unity will cost far more than the government admits. He is right, the voters are not listening, and {party} pays
The Two Plus Four treaty settles Germany's borders and sovereignty, and Genscher's diplomacy is {party}'s strongest card
The Constitutional Court rules that the 5 percent threshold applies separately in East and West, a lifeline for {party}
In the East's state elections on October 14 the CDU wins four of the five new states, and {party} arrives at the federal vote with momentum
'Everyone is talking about Germany, we are talking about the weather': the West Greens campaign on climate while the country talks unity, and {party} pays
Eastern factories begin to close as the new currency prices out their exports, and voters in the East look for a party that speaks for them, such as {party}
Iraq's invasion of Kuwait and the Gulf crisis raise fuel prices and security questions, and the debate favours {party}'s steadiness

issues.name: The cost of unity
issues.blurb: Unity came on October 3, and Kohl promises it without tax rises while Lafontaine warns of a huge bill.

issues.name: Jobs in the East
issues.blurb: Monetary union at one to one, the Treuhand and eastern factories closing as their markets vanish.

issues.name: Social union
issues.blurb: West German pensions and social insurance extended to the East in July, and who will pay for them.

issues.name: Housing shortage
issues.blurb: West German cities short of homes as East Germans and ethnic German resettlers move west.

issues.name: Environment
issues.blurb: The West Greens campaign on the climate, while the East counts the cost of brown coal and dirty rivers.

issues.name: Resettlers & asylum
issues.blurb: Nearly 400,000 ethnic German resettlers this year and close to 200,000 asylum claims.

issues.name: Borders & alliances
issues.blurb: The Two Plus Four treaty, the Oder-Neisse border and a united Germany inside NATO.

1994.label: 1994 · Kohl v. Scharping
1994.tagline: Autumn 1994. Nineteen elections in one year, and Kohl has come back from far behind in the polls. The economy is turning, the East is recovering unevenly, and the SPD has a candidate it has not made up its mind about, flanked by Lafontaine and Schröder. The PDS needs only three direct seats to stay in the Bundestag.

events.headline: In the superelection year nineteen votes keep every party in permanent campaign mode, and {party}'s steady record helps it most
The economy leaves recession and Kohl claims the credit for the upswing. It lifts {party}
The SPD's troika of Scharping, Lafontaine and Schröder gives voters three faces and no clear leader, and {party} pays
The Union's 'red socks' campaign tries to tie the SPD to the PDS. The PDS gets the attention, and {party}'s eastern base loves it
Kohl campaigns tirelessly across the East, pitching the chancellor of unity against the SPD's three-headed team, and {party} holds its eastern lead
In the final week the merged Greens and Bündnis 90 stand clear of the threshold they missed in the West in 1990, and {party} breathes out
The Treuhand's closures and mass unemployment in the East still shape the vote, and {party} pays for the pace of unity
The FDP drops out of one state parliament after another, and {party} fights for the 5 percent line
Three direct seats in East Berlin would keep the PDS in the Bundestag whatever its national score, and {party} campaigns for them street by street

issues.name: Jobs & the upswing
issues.blurb: The economy is out of the 1993 recession, but nearly four million are still out of work.

issues.name: Rebuilding the East
issues.blurb: The Treuhand closes its books at year end, and eastern unemployment stays far above the West's.

issues.name: Asylum & extremism
issues.blurb: The 1993 asylum compromise has cut claims, and the arson attacks in Mölln and Solingen still weigh.

issues.name: Care insurance
issues.blurb: The new long-term care insurance from 1995, paid for in part by giving up a public holiday.

issues.name: Environment
issues.blurb: The Greens' ecological tax reform, nuclear power and the clean-up of the East's rivers and air.

issues.name: Bundeswehr abroad
issues.blurb: The July court ruling allowing Bundeswehr missions abroad, after Somalia and the Adriatic.

1998.label: 1998 · Schröder v. Kohl
1998.tagline: Autumn 1998. After sixteen years, Kohl is asking for another term with unemployment that peaked near five million that winter and an economy that will not move. The SPD has a charismatic candidate from Lower Saxony and a party chairman who does not agree with him on everything. No sitting chancellor has ever been voted out at the ballot box.

events.headline: Schröder wins Lower Saxony in March with 47.9 percent and becomes the SPD's chancellor candidate that night, and {party} has its man
Unemployment tops 4.8 million, a postwar record, and Kohl's talk of recovery rings hollow for {party}
The Greens' conference votes for five marks a litre of petrol, and {party}'s opponents have their campaign gift
Schröder's 'new centre' courts business and the middle class, and {party} wins voters it has not had in years
Gysi's PDS climbs toward 5 percent in the polls on eastern discontent, and {party}'s talk-show turns pay off
In the last week the polls put the SPD ahead and the Union scrambles. Schröder tells Germans it is time for change, and {party} holds on
Sixteen years of the same chancellor wear on {party}, and even its own supporters talk of time for a change
The Schröder and Lafontaine double act gives {party} a leader for the middle and a leader for the base
The FDP campaigns for lower taxes and a firm alliance with the Union, and {party} holds a steady course at about six percent

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: Registered unemployment of 4.8 million last winter, a postwar record, and an economy slow to recover.

issues.name: Pensions & sick pay
issues.blurb: The SPD promises to undo the new pension formula and the cuts to sick pay and protection from dismissal.

issues.name: Reformstau & tax reform
issues.blurb: Kohl's tax reform, blocked by the SPD in the Bundesrat, and the word of 1997: Reformstau.

issues.name: Petrol price & eco-tax
issues.blurb: The Greens' five marks for a litre of petrol and red-green plans for an ecological tax reform.

issues.name: The East
issues.blurb: Eight years after unity, eastern unemployment is about twice the West's and the PDS is gaining.

issues.name: Citizenship
issues.blurb: Red-green plans to ease naturalisation and allow dual citizenship, which the Union opposes.

issues.name: The euro
issues.blurb: Eleven states qualified in May to launch the euro in January, and the end of the D-Mark divides voters.

2002.label: 2002 · Schröder v. Stoiber
2002.tagline: Autumn 2002. Stoiber led all summer, and then the Elbe flooded. Schröder has nearly four million unemployed and a government that has run out of reform, but he also has a war in Iraq he has promised to keep Germany out of. Two televised debates, and nobody is sure of anything until the last week.

events.headline: Stoiber's Union leads by up to ten points through the summer on jobs and a stalled economy, and {party} sets the pace
The Hartz commission reports and Schröder promises to halve unemployment, and {party} has a plan to run on
Floods along the Elbe and in Saxony turn the summer. The chancellor in rubber boots looks like a leader, and {party} gains
Schröder rules out German troops in an Iraq war. It plays well in the East and in the SPD's base, and {party} climbs
Germany's first-ever TV-Duelle split: Stoiber holds his own in the first, Schröder wins the second, and {party} takes back the initiative
Möllemann's flyer attacking Israel's government and Michel Friedman splits the party, and {party}'s 18 percent project stalls in the last week
The justice minister is reported to have compared Bush with Hitler, and Schröder asks her to go. The week is bruising for {party}
Gysi quits as Berlin economics senator over the bonus-miles affair, and the PDS loses its best-known face. {party} feels it in the polls
Fischer is the most popular politician in the country, and the Greens campaign on the vice-chancellor's face. {party} gains

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: Four million out of work, a stalled economy and the Hartz commission's plan to halve joblessness.

issues.name: Iraq
issues.blurb: Schröder rules out German part in a US war on Iraq, and the Union says he is damaging the alliance.

issues.name: The Elbe flood
issues.blurb: The August floods in Saxony and along the Elbe, paid for by postponing next year's income tax cut.

issues.name: Eco-tax & nuclear exit
issues.blurb: The eco-tax on fuel and the nuclear phase-out law, both of which the Union would revisit.

issues.name: Pensions & health
issues.blurb: The new Riester private pension and rising contributions for health and pension insurance.

issues.name: Immigration law
issues.blurb: The immigration law passed in a disputed Bundesrat vote in March, which the Union vows to overturn.

issues.name: The 'Teuro'
issues.blurb: Euro notes and coins arrived in January, and shoppers say prices went up with them.

2005.label: 2005 · Schröder v. Merkel
2005.tagline: Autumn 2005. The chancellor has called an election a year early after losing North Rhine-Westphalia, and he starts far behind. Five million Germans are out of work, the Union is waiting to win, and a new left party under Lafontaine and Gysi has been put together in a hurry.

events.headline: Schröder loses a confidence vote on purpose and calls an early election after the NRW defeat, and {party} starts the race far behind
Lafontaine and Gysi join forces: the PDS renames itself Linkspartei.PDS and opens its lists to the WASG, and {party} surges in the polls
Merkel's tax expert proposes a flat 25 percent income tax, and Schröder mocks the 'professor from Heidelberg'. The lead shrinks for {party}
The Union says it will raise VAT by two points. The 'Merkel tax' gives the SPD a message at last and costs {party} votes
In the only TV-Duell, Schröder comes out ahead on points, and {party} gets a late lift
Union supporters hedge in the final week, and a wave of tactical second votes goes to {party} to secure a black-yellow majority
Lafontaine's 'Fremdarbeiter' remark at a rally in Chemnitz hands the other parties a stick to beat {party} with
Unemployment tops five million and Hartz IV protesters are back on the streets. The reforms that {party} passed are now its burden
Fischer is questioned for hours over the visa affair, and the quarrel dents {party}'s image of competence

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: More than five million registered unemployed in early 2005, the highest count since the war.

issues.name: Hartz IV
issues.blurb: Hartz IV merged unemployment aid with welfare in January, and the new Left Party campaigns against it.

issues.name: Flat tax & VAT
issues.blurb: Kirchhof's 25 percent flat tax and the Union's two-point VAT rise, which the SPD calls the Merkel tax.

issues.name: Health insurance
issues.blurb: The SPD's citizens' insurance for all against the Union's flat health premium per person.

issues.name: Nuclear exit
issues.blurb: The Union and FDP would let nuclear plants run longer, and red-green defends its phase-out law.

issues.name: Turkey & the EU
issues.blurb: EU entry talks with Turkey are due in October, and the Union offers a privileged partnership instead.

2009.label: 2009 · Merkel v. Steinmeier
2009.tagline: Autumn 2009. A grand coalition that worked its way through the financial crash is ending, and nobody in it wants to say so. Merkel runs as the crisis manager, Steinmeier as the man who would like to be, and the smaller parties see the biggest opening in a generation.

events.headline: The scrappage bonus and the Opel rescue talks make crisis management the story of the summer, and {party} stays closest to the factory gates
Three state elections on August 30 show the Left above 20 percent in the East and the SPD still sinking, and {party} rides the wave
The Kunduz air strike kills civilians and reopens the Afghanistan debate, and the questions land on {party}'s government
A polite, sleepy TV-Duell with four moderators. Steinmeier is sharper, Merkel is safer, and {party} keeps its lead
'More net from gross': Westerwelle's tax-cut pitch fills the halls and the polls for {party}
Steinmeier's 'Germany Plan' promises four million new jobs by 2020, and a public tired of the grand coalition shrugs at {party}
The web-blocking law and a new Pirate Party carry young online voters away from the big parties, and {party} picks up the protest
The Union and FDP want longer nuclear plant lifetimes, and the anti-nuclear camp rallies behind {party}
Opel's future is argued out in Berlin in the final weeks, and workers look to {party} to save the plants

issues.name: Financial crisis
issues.blurb: The worst recession since the war, short-time work, the scrappage bonus, the bank rescues and Opel.

issues.name: Tax cuts
issues.blurb: The FDP's 'more net from gross' and the Union's tax cut pledges, against record new borrowing.

issues.name: Nuclear power
issues.blurb: The Union and FDP want longer lives for nuclear plants, and the SPD and Greens defend the phase-out.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: The new guarantee that pensions will never be cut, and retirement at 67 starting in 2012.

issues.name: Minimum wage
issues.blurb: The SPD's call for a general legal minimum wage, against the Union's minimums for single sectors.

issues.name: Afghanistan
issues.blurb: The Kunduz air strike of September 4 and how long the Bundeswehr should stay in Afghanistan.

issues.name: Internet freedom
issues.blurb: The web-blocking law and data retention, which bring a new Pirate Party onto the ballot.

2013.label: 2013 · Merkel v. Steinbrück
2013.tagline: Autumn 2013. Merkel is the most trusted politician in the country and the euro crisis has made her Europe's safest pair of hands. The FDP is polling on the threshold, a new anti-euro party has appeared from nowhere, and everyone below the Union is fighting for second place or for survival.

events.headline: Floods on the Elbe and the Danube put the chancellor in the disaster zone, and her calm crisis management earns {party} the week
Snowden's NSA files dominate the summer, and the claim that the affair is over leaves {party}'s government on the defensive
The Greens' plan for a weekly meat-free day in canteens becomes the campaign's favourite punchline, and {party} spends August explaining it
Merkel and Steinbrück meet in the only TV-Duell. The chancellor keeps her cool and {party} takes a narrow win on points
A magazine cover shows Steinbrück with his middle finger raised, and the image follows {party}'s candidate for days
Bavaria votes a week early. The CSU wins an absolute majority and the FDP drops out of the Landtag, so the threshold panic reaches {party}
A party founded this year campaigns against the bailouts and the euro, and {party} collects the protest vote from both flanks
The Greens' 1980s debates about sex with minors resurface in the final weeks, and {party}'s Trittin has to explain a 1981 local programme
The FDP begs Union voters to lend it their second votes. The pitch only half works for {party}
A statutory minimum wage of 8.50 euros becomes the centrepiece of the left's pitch, and {party} gets the pay debate it wanted

issues.name: Economy & jobs
issues.blurb: Unemployment under three million and exports booming while much of Europe is in recession.

issues.name: Euro crisis
issues.blurb: Bailouts for Greece, the ESM rescue fund and German liability, and a new AfD that wants the euro wound up.

issues.name: Minimum wage
issues.blurb: SPD, Greens and Left want a legal minimum of 8.50 euros an hour, and the Union prefers deals by sector.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: Higher pensions for mothers of children born before 1992, and the SPD's call for retirement at 63.

issues.name: Energiewende & power bills
issues.blurb: The post-Fukushima nuclear exit and a renewables surcharge that keeps raising household power bills.

issues.name: Taxes
issues.blurb: SPD and Greens plan a 49 percent top rate and a wealth levy, and the Union rules out any tax rise.

issues.name: Rents & the rent brake
issues.blurb: Rents rising fast in the big cities, and a rent brake that both big parties now promise.

issues.name: NSA & privacy
issues.blurb: Snowden's files on US surveillance in Germany and what the government knew about it.

2017.label: 2017 · Merkel v. Schulz
2017.tagline: Autumn 2017. The Schulz train has run out of track, the grand coalition drags on, and for the first time a party of the hard right is heading for the Bundestag. Merkel's fourth term is not the question. Who comes second, and who comes third, is.

events.headline: The Schulz train derails: the SPD candidate's spring surge fades into a summer of state-election defeats, and {party} can't find a second wind
'Merkel muss weg': the migration backlash after 2015 hardens into votes, and {party} owns the anger
The one and only TV-Duell: a cautious, consensual night that changes almost nothing, and {party}'s challenger fails to land a blow
Back from the dead: Lindner's slick, yellow-and-magenta relaunch puts {party} over the 5% line and then some
'Wir werden sie jagen': a deliberately provocative closing pitch rallies {party}'s base and clears the way to third place
The eastern fight for the protest vote turns brutal, and {party} loses ground to the newcomers on its old home turf
'Sie kennen mich': the steady-hand incumbency pitch reassures the middle, and {party} coasts
Grand-coalition fatigue drains the life out of {party}'s base: why vote for the junior partner of the status quo?
A late realo-flügel push and a slick ground game hold {party} safely over the threshold

issues.name: Refugees & integration
issues.blurb: More than a million asylum seekers since 2015, deportations and the CSU's demanded cap of 200,000 a year.

issues.name: Economy & diesel
issues.blurb: Record employment and a budget surplus, with the diesel emissions scandal hanging over the car industry.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: How to stop the pension level falling as the baby boomers retire, and whether to work past 67.

issues.name: Social justice
issues.blurb: Schulz's call for more fairness: low wages, fixed-term contracts and the legacy of Agenda 2010.

issues.name: Climate & coal
issues.blurb: Germany set to miss its 2020 climate target, the date to stop burning coal and diesel driving bans.

issues.name: Rents
issues.blurb: Rents still climbing in Berlin, Munich and Hamburg despite the 2015 rent brake.

issues.name: Security & terrorism
issues.blurb: The Berlin Christmas market attack of December 2016, police powers and Trump's demands on NATO spending.

2021.label: 2021 · Scholz v. Laschet
2021.tagline: Autumn 2021. Merkel is leaving after sixteen years, the Ahr valley is still digging out of the flood, and for the first time in the republic's history the chancellery has no incumbent and no favourite. Three candidates, one open throne.

events.headline: Cameras catch Laschet laughing behind the President in the flood zone, and the clip is everywhere
The CV-and-plagiarism summer catches up with Baerbock again
Scholz wins the third Triell in a row. Who else?
Ampel or Jamaika? Final-week coalition arithmetic pulls tactical voters toward {party}
The 'Scholzomat' steady-hand surge: boring is the new electable for {party}
Cum-ex and Wirecard questions dog {party}'s candidate, but never quite land
First-time voters break for {party} as the yellow wave runs through every school gym
{party} stares down the 5% cliff. Only three direct mandates can save the list
A red-red-green scare campaign rallies the {party} base in the final stretch

issues.name: Climate protection
issues.blurb: After the Ahr valley flood: the coal exit date, the CO2 price and the court ruling against the climate law.

issues.name: Economy & debt
issues.blurb: Recovery from the pandemic slump and whether to restore the debt brake after record borrowing.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: Holding the pension level at 48 percent and whether the retirement age should rise beyond 67.

issues.name: Rents & housing
issues.blurb: Berlin's rent cap, struck down in April, and the city's vote on expropriating large landlords.

issues.name: The pandemic
issues.blurb: A fourth COVID wave, the vaccination campaign and the cost of lockdowns for schools and shops.

issues.name: Minimum wage
issues.blurb: The SPD's pledge to lift the minimum wage from 9.60 euros to 12 euros an hour.

issues.name: Afghanistan & refugees
issues.blurb: The fall of Kabul in August, the airlift and how many Afghans Germany should take in.

2025.label: 2025 · Merz v. Scholz
2025.tagline: Winter 2025. The traffic-light coalition has collapsed, the economy is in its second year of recession, and the AfD polls second. Hold the centre, or ride the revolt.

events.headline: Musk endorses the AfD and livestreams with Weidel. The base roars, the centre recoils
The Aschaffenburg attack reignites the migration debate, and {party} owns the week
Merz's migration motion passes with AfD votes, and the hardline base rallies to {party}
Hundreds of thousands march against the firewall breach. Merkel rebukes Merz, and the centre flinches from {party}
{party}'s chancellor candidate takes the TV-Duell on points
VW plant closures and a second year of recession put the economy minister on trial, and {party} bleeds
'Worst result since 1887': the doom loop tightens around {party}
BSW and FDP flirt with the 5% line, and wasted-vote warnings squeeze {party}
Habeck's kitchen-table campaign finds its audience, a quiet lift for {party}

issues.name: Migration
issues.blurb: Asylum numbers, rejections at the border and the attacks in Solingen, Magdeburg and Aschaffenburg.

issues.name: Economy & industry
issues.blurb: Two years of recession, job cuts at VW and the price of energy for German industry.

issues.name: Ukraine & defence
issues.blurb: Arms for Ukraine, the Taurus missile, the 100 billion euro Bundeswehr fund and NATO's spending target.

issues.name: Pensions
issues.blurb: The pension package that died with the coalition, the 48 percent level and who pays as boomers retire.

issues.name: Debt brake & taxes
issues.blurb: The coalition broke in November over a budget gap and the debt brake, and the Union promises tax cuts.

issues.name: Energy & heating
issues.blurb: Power prices, the 2023 heating law and how fast to move off gas and coal.

issues.name: Rents
issues.blurb: City rents and whether to extend the rent brake beyond the end of 2025.

events.headline: Grim industrial numbers dominate the news, putting pressure on {party}
A border incident reignites the migration debate, and {party} owns the airwaves
{party}'s leader wins the TV-Duell on points
A firewall row over voting with the far right bruises {party}
Coalition-arithmetic anxiety drives tactical voters toward {party}
A funding scandal engulfs a {party} candidate
A social-media wave breaks for {party} among young voters
{party}'s leader fumbles a live interview
Business leaders and papers line up behind {party}
A security shock puts statesmanship first, and {party} looks the part
The networks offer {party} a TV-Duell slot
events.prompt: A head-to-head is on the table. How do you play it?

choices.text: Accept and go on the attack
choices.resultText: You land blows and take a few. The overnight polls twitch your way.
A steady, on-message night. No gaffes, no fireworks.

choices.text: Decline: protect the lead, avoid the ambush
choices.resultText: You dodge the studio lights. The press calls it caution.

events.headline: {party} faces a firewall question that won't go away
events.prompt: How do you handle the Brandmauer?

choices.text: Draw a hard line: no deals, no votes
choices.resultText: The centre breathes easier. Your right flank fumes.

choices.text: Keep it ambiguous, case by case
choices.resultText: Everyone hears what they want. Trust erodes a little.

choices.text: Turn it into an attack on the rival
choices.resultText: You change the subject, and it mostly works.

events.headline: {party}'s programme committee is split on the big pledge
events.prompt: The draft is ready. Which way do you push?

choices.text: Go bold with a defining, risky pledge
choices.resultText: The base roars. The spreadsheets at HQ look nervous.

choices.text: Play it cautious: no hostages to fortune
Make it a contrast document against the rival
choices.resultText: You define them more than yourself, and it lands.
